A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same C-Nav study, with readable text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C. All scientific content can be matched; v3's additional page results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original HM3D and MP3D navigation experiments across four architectures, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and additional analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original navigation experiments, numerical comparisons, ablations, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The feature-distillation and feature-replay paths, CLIP/LOF experience selection, training objective, and architecture implementations are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendix B, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same continual ObjectNav coverage on HM3D and MP3D, with six and 21 object categories respectively. No dataset, task, population, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain Finetuning, LoRA, LwF, Merge, and data replay. VLFM remains in Figure 6, and uniform/clustering sampling comparators remain in Figure 5. The newly cited VLMs are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The four-stage splits, sample counts, SR/SPL metrics, 500-step episode limit, architecture configurations, and training settings match in Section 3, Table 1, Section 5.1, and Appendix B.

E4.justification: Both retain the same component ablations, sampling and retention-ratio comparisons, stage-order sensitivity, navigation case study, old/new-task analysis, encoder-freezing analysis, and loss-weight sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and Appendix C.

E5.justification: Both use the same point estimates and stage/architecture averages. Neither reports random-seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The numerical results, plotted trends, and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 2 retains C-Nav's HM3D-Bev average/final SR of 56.3/46.5, and Table 7 retains its final old-task SR of 42.61.

T1.justification: Section 3's formal task definitions and Section 4's losses, distance definitions, and LOF equations (1–6) are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, dual-path anti-forgetting, and adaptive experience-selection contributions, together with the same performance and memory-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of representation drift, policy forgetting, and stability–plasticity remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning physical-robot validation, lighting and sensor noise, and storage growing with task complexity.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix B retain the same implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and pseudocode. Both promise future code availability at the same project address; deleting 'publicly' does not establish an access change.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 adds NVILA and Qwen2.5-VL to the VLM citations and moves the retained Qwen technical-report citation into the LLM group. This modestly expands cited background without changing the research positioning or novelty claims.

P1.justification: v3 revises bibliographic metadata and formatting, consolidates duplicate LoRA and Habitat-Web entries, and updates citation numbering. It also removes 'publicly' from the code sentence and replaces the preprint footer with NeurIPS 2025 information. The narrative and section structure otherwise match.

P2.justification: The first-page footer changes and the bibliography reflows onto an additional page, shifting the appendices. Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–8 retain their designs, captions, and organization; matched appendix page bodies are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves v1's conflicting duplicate LoRA entries, consolidates duplicate Habitat-Web references, and adds relevant VLM citations. These changes modestly improve reference consistency and coverage. The method, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, so the quality gain is limited.
